h: Chelmsford climbers, here's your game plan
p: Sixty-odd minutes of climbing sounds like plenty until you're actually in it. Suddenly the timer's ticking and there are still five walls you haven't tried. The trick is to go in with a rough plan. Warm up on a couple of easier challenges, then hit the speed walls while your arms are fresh, and leave the big drops and jumps until the end when the nerves have settled.

Before the day, sort the participation forms. Every climber needs one, and parents or guardians sign for under-18s. Doing them online beforehand makes check-in quick. Have a look at the age rules too, as there's usually a minimum age for climbers and guidance on supervising little ones.
Allow a couple of hours for the whole visit, eat something light beforehand and bring water. Nails short, rings off, phones handed to whoever's watching from the side.

If you've got time to fill afterwards, Chelmsford Museum sits in Oaklands Park with local history, natural history and a good play area outside, and Central Park by the river is handy for a stroll near the city centre. Chelmsford Cathedral is worth a quick look if you're passing. For a longer outing, RHS Garden Hyde Hall lies a short drive south-east of the city, with big skies and gorgeous planting that's a world away from the climbing walls.
